requirements.text: As a user, I want the system to provide clear error messages when an operation fails, so that I can understand what went wrong and how to fix it.
requirements.rationale: The speaker explicitly states a need for clear error messages, which is a functional requirement for user guidance.

requirements.text: The system shall retain saved articles, personal notes, and submission records until explicitly deleted by the user.
requirements.rationale: Managing personal interactions over time implies data persistence, and no retention limits were mentioned, so indefinite retention with user deletion is a reasonable assumption.

requirements.text: As an author, I want the system to send email notifications when the status of my submitted article changes (e.g., under review, accepted, rejected), so that I am informed without having to manually check.
requirements.rationale: The user story about tracking submission status implies a notification mechanism; email is the standard external channel for such updates.

requirements.text: As a user, I want to authenticate before accessing my personal library, saved articles, notes, and submission tracking, so that only I can view and manage my personal data.
requirements.rationale: The system stores personal data (saved articles, notes, submission status) which requires user authentication to protect privacy and ensure access control.

requirements.text: As a user, I want my personal notes and highlights on articles to be visible only to me, so that my private annotations remain confidential.
requirements.rationale: Personal notes and highlights are private user data; access must be restricted to the owning user to comply with data protection principles.

requirements.text: As a system administrator, I want an audit log of all access to personal user data (saved articles, notes, submission status) and any changes made, so that we can detect unauthorized access and comply with regulatory requirements.
requirements.rationale: Handling personal data necessitates an audit trail for security monitoring and regulatory compliance (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA if applicable).

requirements.text: The system shall encrypt all personal user data (saved articles, notes, submission status) at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption (e.g., TLS for transit, AES-256 for storage).
requirements.rationale: Encryption is a baseline security control to protect personal data from unauthorized access and comply with data protection regulations.

requirements.text: As a user, I want to give explicit consent for the system to store and process my personal data (such as notes, bookmarks, submission history) before I can use those features, so that my privacy rights are respected.
requirements.rationale: Collecting personal data requires user consent under privacy regulations like GDPR; the system must obtain it before processing.

requirements.text: As a user, I want to be able to delete my account and all associated personal data (saved articles, notes, submission history), so that I can exercise my right to erasure.
requirements.rationale: Privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR) grant users the right to deletion; the system must provide this capability for personal data.

requirements.text: As a reader, I want to take notes on articles, so that I can record my thoughts and observations while reading papers.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly mentions 'taking notes on them' as a desired interaction when asked to describe specific interactions.

requirements.text: As a reader, I want to save or bookmark articles of interest to a personal library, so that I can easily return to them later.
requirements.rationale: The analyst explicitly stated this user story as part of managing personal interactions, which Spk 1 confirmed.

requirements.text: As a potential author, I want the system to accept article submissions, so that authors can contribute to the publication.
requirements.rationale: User Story 6 explicitly states submitting a new research article, which requires a submission interface within the system.

requirements.text: As a potential author, I want to submit a new research article to the journal, so that I can contribute to the publication.
requirements.rationale: The analyst inferred this requirement from the general concept of 'managing my involvement with the journal' and tracking submissions.

requirements.text: As a reader, I want to add personal notes or highlights to an article I am reading, so that I can annotate important sections for my own reference.
requirements.rationale: The analyst explicitly stated this user story based on Spk 1's desire to manage personal interactions.

requirements.text: As an author, I want to track the status of my submitted articles (e.g., under review, accepted, rejected), so that I am informed of the editorial process.
requirements.rationale: The analyst inferred this requirement from the need to manage interactions and the submission tracking mentioned in the conversation.

requirements.text: As a reader, I want to browse and search a catalog of medical research articles, so that I can find papers relevant to my interests.
requirements.rationale: The analyst explicitly stated this user story after Spk 1 confirmed the desire to read papers.

requirements.text: As a reader, I want to view the full text and details of a medical research article, so that I can read and learn from it.
requirements.rationale: The analyst explicitly stated this user story based on Spk 1's stated need to read papers.

requirements.text: As a reader, I want to view and manage my collection of saved articles and personal notes in one place, so that I can organize my research.
requirements.rationale: The analyst explicitly stated this user story as a consolidation of the bookmarking and annotation features.

requirements.text: As an author, I want to track articles I have submitted for publication, so that I can monitor their status and history.
requirements.rationale: The speaker explicitly asks about tracking submitted articles, indicating a need for author-specific functionality.
